items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: it was there that I saw Mamie Smith, Ma Rainey and Bessie Smith... I also worked for one week at this show place.

ctx.x: My father left Cincinnati to work in another city and I started enjoying myself in the shooting gallery to the extent that I stopped going to band rehearsals. As my mother never worried about what I did when I was out of the house, I was my own little man. The result of my not going to the rehearsals was that Mr. Ernest Moore came to the house one day and took the horn. I was not interested in playing music.

Another movie and vaudeville house opened on Central Avenue between 4th and 5th Streets and it was there that I saw Mamie Smith, Ma Rainey and Bessie Smith, the most famous of all the women blues singers. I also worked for one week at this show place. There was a part in the show about a man, his wife and their many children coming from the South to visit some relatives in the North. There must have been about 10 of us and all living in Hathaway Street. We did two shows a day and were very proud that we were…

The Whitman Sisters show was another one that came very often to Cincinnati. I do not remember anything interesting concerning the musical background of the show but Alice Whitman was the first woman tap dancer that I had ever seen and she was a great one.
